title: Egg, whole, fried no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: A whole egg fried without added fat is a standard chicken egg cooked on a dry skillet. This method retains most nutrients while delivering a low‑calorie, protein‑rich dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most complete foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Frying without oil creates a crisp exterior without extra calories.
Eggs provide more vitamin D than most plant‑based foods.
They are widely used as a binding and leavening agent in cooking.
USDA defines a "large" egg as the standard serving size.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A large egg supplies about 6 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin (B2) and biotin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Choline
items.content: Choline in the yolk is important for liver function and cognitive processes.

items.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These carotenoids help protect eye health and may reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk is high in cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume eggs in moderation.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella. Fry until the white is fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried eggs without added fat can be enjoyed on their own, added to salads, sandwiches, rice or vegetable dishes. Cook on medium heat for a softer texture or high heat for a crispy edge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep eggs refrigerated at 1‑4 °C in their original carton. Use within 3‑5 days of purchase. Cooked eggs should be stored in the fridge and eaten within 2 days.
